CHEMISTRY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrochemistry ● Redox reactions ● Electrochemical cell ● Standard electrode p? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrochemistry ● Redox reactions ● Electrochemical cell ● Standard electrode p.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrochemistry ● Redox reactions ● Electrochemical cell ● Standard electrode p.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Electrochemistry ● Redox reactions ● Electrochemical cell ● Standard electrode p.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrochemistry ● Redox reactions ● Electrochemical cell ● Standard electrode p.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrochemistry 2.3 Nuclear chemistry 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Alkanols 3.2 Al.

5. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Glucose and oxygen

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nuclear Chemistry ● Stability of isotopes ● Chemical and nuclear reactions ● Rad? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nuclear Chemistry ● Stability of isotopes ● Chemical and nuclear reactions ● Rad.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nuclear Chemistry ● Stability of isotopes ● Chemical and nuclear reactions ● Rad.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Nuclear Chemistry ● Stability of isotopes ● Chemical and nuclear reactions ● Rad.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nuclear Chemistry ● Stability of isotopes ● Chemical and nuclear reactions ● Rad.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY Strand S? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY Strand S.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY Strand S.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY Strand S.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Detergents 3.4 Polymers Page 12 of 40 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY Strand S.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Detergents ● Types of detergents ● Preparation of detergents ● Mode of action of.

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes ● System and surrounding ● Ene.

11. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes 2.2. Electrochemistry 2.3 Nucl? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes 2.2. Electrochemistry 2.3 Nucl.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy Changes in physical and chemical processes 2.2. Electrochemistry 2.3 Nucl.

----
